summary: On SailAway 2 (69% sea) the player made hovers the side's army: a hover platform on every seat, then Goons, Caymans and Mangonels. It announced 'Going hovers' in chat and took the islands well: 54 extractors across the side at 9:00-10:00, against 10 of his seen all game. thebluegecko (Cortex) went navy: Riptides from 4:10, a sonar tower going up at the G5 crossing at 5:50, subs from about 8:52 that nothing of ours could see or hit, Cutlass seaplanes from 10:11 and Buccaneers at 21:23. Our answer to the first Riptide was more hovers and one shipyard on the water seat; the Goons chased ships that kite, and the 7:24 push across the sea to his commander (seen once) arrived at 10:05-10:51, just as the Cutlasses did: 7.8k lost for 1.1k in minute 10. Subs then took the shipyard, the naval hover platform and the water seat's commander (12:22). The side's extractors fell from 51 at 12:00 to 24 at 16:00 with 3-5k banked, and from 15:40 a fleet of 10-14 Riptides beat the Mangonel body at home; we lost 75.2k for 20.6k seen and resigned at 24:33 after thebluegecko called it unwinnable.

bears_on.note: This game is the lesson's source. 102 of our 217 combat hovers were Mangonels, and from 15:40 they were the body at home against Riptides: 'Two Riptides at F6 have killed ~10 Mangonels in 3 min' (16:04).
Hovers as army bulk (217 combat hovers built, 194 lost) lost to a navy. The user's 24:11 'I am told hovers are bad generically' is the earlier form of the human-17 lesson.
He answered a hover mass with what it could not fight: Riptides that outrun Mangonels and Caymans, subs no hover can target, and Cutlasses the Mangonels cannot shoot.

This bounds the lesson. At 7:00 our army was 6.8k against 1.15k of his seen, and going to use it (7:24) lost 7.8k for 1.1k. The lead was in units that could not catch his ships or hit his subs and seaplanes, and his army was a floor.

On what we saw, we held 54 extractors at 10:00 against his 10 seen and lost on the unit domain. The collapse to 24 at 16:00 was a cost of the mix, not the cause. His real count is unknown (no truth file).

At 7:24 the player sent every soldier at a commander seen once, about 7,400 from the red home across the sea. The army arrived at 10:05-10:51; his commander, seen at E1 at 10:46, killed two Caymans and lived.
A day after the lesson, our player announced its seats and plan at 0:22 ('Going hovers') and the push at 7:42. He answered 'i see them' at 7:52; whether it changed his play is not shown.
The user's 0:53 word set the water seat's first energy, a tidal at 1:04, after a 794-elmo walk toward a wind site that did not exist.

Seat 0's first three Goons crossed at 3:52-3:59 and died at 4:25-5:04 to his first Herring, an LLT and a construction ship; on a sea map the first handful meets ships. Later rovers lived longer, and one found his commander at D1 at 7:23.
The 'one body' push strung out: group_A_t2 '89 s near home, 8371 to go' at 9:28, with its tail 2,600 behind at 15:11.

lens.caveats: There is no truth file, batch.json or results.jsonl, so all his numbers are floors (subs and seaplanes mostly out of sight). The per-match tools read record-0 only; seats 1 and 2 were run through scratchpad symlink directories. minutes.py's 'he starts F6' is the snap bug's guess, which voids its 'his half' columns and the 8:00-11:00 and 13:00-15:00 windows. analyze_match's army column now counts hovers, but its engagement 'on the spot' soldier values are still 0 for them. pro_baseline.py was not run (Comet only). chat.jsonl marks the host lines '?'; they are attributed here to the user (computer_whisperer) by the host-seat rule in design §6 and docs/knowledge/_inbox/players-chat-2026-09-28.md. The date is 2026-09-27 by the batch's epoch and the files; the brief passage and the lessons give 2026-09-28, the relay date. Where I differ from review.md and the ledger: (1) The root clock is 0:00, the plan, with 4:23 as the last cheap switch, and I name a harness share they do not: the water block's list had no ship. (2) The review's Z1 stands against the ledger: bot.log has 'the prompt on disk has changed' twice, and impedance_sweep counts 3 session replacements (6:48, 15:11 cap, 19:46). (3) The 4:23 '650' was the Herring's range, given in the same report line, not a header misread. (4) The 24:24 refusal of 'remove commander_t2' was its death to a Buccaneer at 24:24, not a naming fault. (5) His commander was at E1 at 10:46 and killed two Caymans at 10:51-10:53, so 'commander not there' (10:43) was true only by seconds. (6) The second push (12:47 gather_e3, 14:44 his_commander) during the 12-16 extractor collapse is a finding the review folds into air and subs.

Did the water block's hover-only list (no ship or shipyard) steer the 0:00 'hovers cross water'? It is still so in briefing.rs. An offline replay of the 0:00 turn with ships listed would tell.

What would have held: Riptides of our own from 4:23 on two seats plus sonar towers and Urchins at each harbour? Game 12 (shipyards on every seat by 1:09) lost too, on reach per the brief, so 'a navy' alone is not the whole answer.
Did the fresh session at 6:48 (brief edited on disk) change the plan? The 7:24 push was the second session's, built on the carried notes; the transcript cannot separate the two.
Were the 27 engine refusals of cormex sites (G3, F3, H3, D3, E2 from 5:30) his extractors already standing on spots of his half, i.e. constructors sent to taken spots?
Is the 'spot_11 is not a place in the picture' refusal for an under-water spot before any hover constructor stands still open, as the ledger says?
